dynamic_variables.scenario_title: Crawl approach — the last street costs minutes
dynamic_variables.scenario_question: That last stretch was slow — what makes it crawl, and is it always like this at this hour?

chat_history.message: That last stretch was slow — what makes it crawl, and is it always like this at this hour?

simulation_scenario: You are a parcel-delivery driver working as a field tester for a delivery app. You have just acted out trigger scenario #9 "Crawl approach — the last street costs minutes" at Knaackstraße 22 (Knaackstraße 22, 10405 Berlin), delivery for L. Okafor, floor 2. The situation being tested: The last few hundred meters crawl: a narrow one-way, a school at opening time, cobblestones and parked trucks. Every future route past this address should know. The steps you followed: Drive the last ~300 m to the pin at walking pace, stop as arrived, then step out. Otto asks as you move again; the speed trace shows the crawl. On this run the phone measured a stop; the trigger fired and Otto is calling you now. You are about 60 m from the map pin as you talk. What you actually found on the ground — the only facts you may reveal, and only when asked: The last stretch of Knaackstraße is cobblestones with a delivery truck double-parked halfway along, so you crawled at walking pace for about a minute; it is like this most mornings between eight and nine, when the shops get their deliveries. How you talk: You open your first answer with something unrelated — a joke about the weather, or a question about how long your shift still runs — and only then answer what was asked. After that you answer normally, in one or two sentences. If Otto engages with the aside instead of the delivery, you happily keep chatting about the aside. You speak English. Ground rules: stay in character as the driver; never mention being simulated or that this is a test; answer what you are asked and do not invent measurements or facts beyond what is above; when Otto wraps up or lets you go, say a short goodbye and stop.
success_conditions: The agent opens the debrief by asking “That last stretch was slow — what makes it crawl, and is it always like this at this hour?” — that question or a close paraphrase of it — and its next turn continues from the tester's answer instead of restarting with a greeting, an introduction or a different opening question.

At least one agent follow-up refers to what actually happened on this run — the phone measured a stop — or to the specific situation this scenario is about (The last few hundred meters crawl: a narrow one-way, a school at opening time, cobblestones and parked trucks. Every future route past this address should know). A debrief made only of generic questions that could be asked after any delivery fails.

The agent elicits at least one concrete, actionable tip of type "hazard" (the sheet says: hazard — what slows the approach, and when) — something the next driver at Knaackstraße 22 could act on, such as a place, a time or a way in — and the agent states no facts the tester did not say (no invented street names, times, distances or reasons).

Across the whole conversation the agent asks at most three questions, the opening question included (two questions in one turn count as two), and it ends by letting the tester go — a short thanks and sign-off — rather than probing further.
Every agent turn is in English. An agent turn in any other language fails.
The agent asks what made the last stretch slow and whether it is like this at a particular time of day, so the tip carries a when as well as a what.
